evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/auth.rs:97 — AuthService::generate_token() does `rng.try_fill_bytes(&mut bytes).expect("OS rng failed")`. generate_token() mints email-verification and password-reset tokens, so it runs on live request paths (auth handlers). An OsRng/SysRng fill failure therefore panics inside the request task instead of returning an AuthError, aborting the request ungracefully rather than yielding a clean 500.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/oauth.rs:914-919 — OAuthService::generate_random_b64() has the identical `rand::rngs::SysRng.try_fill_bytes(&mut bytes).expect("OS rng failed")`, and per its own doc comment (L908-910) it backs generate_secure_token(), register_client / regenerate_client_secret (client secret), and register_client (client id) — all request-path OAuth operations.

The divergence is internal to this same service layer: the sibling totp.rs (services/totp.rs:149-155) handles the EXACT same SysRng.try_fill_bytes failure gracefully, mapping it to `TotpError::EncryptionError(format!("secure RNG failed to generate nonce: {e}"))` rather than panicking. auth.rs and oauth.rs should follow totp.rs and return their existing error type (AuthError / an OAuth error) on RNG failure so a CSPRNG fault degrades to a handled 500 instead of a panicked task abort.

Severity low: an OS CSPRNG fill failure is extraordinarily rare and arguably unrecoverable, so this is a robustness/consistency smell, not a live crash under normal input. Confidence medium: the panic path and the request-path reachability are certain by static read, but triggering it requires an OS RNG failure that cannot be reproduced statically. candidate_vector bug (recoverable-error vs panic), not test/perf.
